questions.question_text:
Two earthquakes have magnitudes $6$ and $3$.
Richter magnitude is given by $M=\log_{10}A$.
How many times greater is the ground amplitude of the magnitude-$6$ earthquake?

options.why: Used the magnitude difference $6-3=3$ as the amplitude ratio instead of calculating $10^{3}$.
Divided the magnitudes, calculating $6/3=2$, instead of comparing their amplitudes.
Used a magnitude difference of $1$ instead of the actual difference of $3$.

questions.solution_text:
$A_{6}=10^{6}$
$A_{3}=10^{3}$
$\dfrac{A_{6}}{A_{3}}=\dfrac{10^{6}}{10^{3}}=1000$
The magnitude-$6$ earthquake has $1000$ times the ground amplitude.

questions.question_text:
Sound level is given by $S=10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_{0}}$.
A machine measures $30$ dB.
How many times greater is its sound intensity than the threshold of human hearing?

options.why: Divided $30$ by $10$ but used the resulting logarithm as the intensity ratio.
Used the decibel reading directly as the intensity ratio.
Raised $10$ to the decibel reading without first dividing the reading by $10$.

questions.question_text:
One solution has a pH of $2$ and another has a pH of $7$.
Using $M=10^{-pH}$, how many times greater is the hydrogen-ion concentration of the pH-$2$ solution?

options.why: Reversed the concentration ratio, calculating $10^{-7}/10^{-2}$.
Used the pH difference $7-2=5$ as the concentration ratio.
Divided the pH readings, calculating $7/2=3.5$, instead of comparing the concentrations.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{M_{2}}{M_{7}}=\dfrac{10^{-2}}{10^{-7}}$
$=10^{5}$
$=100\,000$
The pH-$2$ solution has $100\,000$ times the hydrogen-ion concentration.

questions.question_text:
Star magnitude is given by $m=-2.5\log_{10}\dfrac{B}{B_{0}}$, where $B$ is brightness and $B_{0}$ is a fixed reference brightness.
Two stars have magnitudes $3.5$ and $6.0$.
How many times brighter is the magnitude-$3.5$ star than the magnitude-$6.0$ star?

options.why: Divided the magnitude difference $6.0-3.5=2.5$ by $2.5$ but used the resulting logarithm as the brightness ratio.
Calculated $10^{2.5}=316.227766\ldots$ without dividing the magnitude difference by the scale multiplier $2.5$.
Reversed the brightness ratio, calculating $10^{(3.5-6.0)/2.5}=0.1$.

questions.question_text:
One air-conditioning unit measures $54$ dB and another measures $44$ dB.
Using $S=10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_{0}}$, how many times greater is the sound intensity of the louder unit?

options.why: Divided the decibel difference by $10$ but used the resulting logarithm as the intensity ratio.
Used a decibel difference of $20$ instead of the actual difference of $10$.
Reversed the intensity ratio, calculating $10^{(44-54)/10}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{I_{54}}{I_{44}}=\dfrac{10^{54/10}}{10^{44/10}}$
$=10^{1}$
$=10$
The louder unit has $10$ times the sound intensity.

options.why: Read the rise of $2$ on the logarithmic axis as the growth factor itself.
Divided the final reading $5$ by the starting reading $3$ instead of subtracting them.
Multiplied the rise of $2$ by $10$ rather than raising $10$ to that power.

questions.solution_text:
At $t=0$ the graph reads $3$ and at $t=40$ it reads $5$.
$5-3=2$
$\dfrac{V_{40}}{V_{0}}=10^{2}$
$=100$
The investment grew to $100$ times its starting value.

questions.question_text:
Richter magnitude is given by $M=\log_{10}A$, where $A$ is the ground amplitude.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $100$ times the ground amplitude of a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has twice the ground amplitude of a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
options.why: Used the magnitude difference $7-5=2$ as the amplitude ratio instead of calculating $10^{2}$.

options.text: A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $10$ times the ground amplitude of a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
options.why: Used a magnitude difference of $1$ rather than the actual difference of $2$.

options.text: A magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $2$ more units of ground amplitude than a magnitude-$5$ earthquake.
options.why: Read the difference in magnitude as a difference in amplitude rather than as an index.

questions.solution_text:
$7-5=2$
$\dfrac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}=10^{2}$
$=100$
The magnitude-$7$ earthquake has $100$ times the ground amplitude.

questions.question_text:
A workshop tool measures $77$ dB and a quieter tool measures $71$ dB.
Using $S=10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_{0}}$, how many times greater is the sound intensity of the louder tool, correct to one decimal place?

options.why: Divided the decibel difference $6$ by $10$ but used the resulting logarithm as the intensity ratio.
Used the decibel difference $77-71=6$ directly as the intensity ratio.
Calculated $10^{6}$ without dividing the decibel difference by $10$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{I_{77}}{I_{71}}=\dfrac{10^{77/10}}{10^{71/10}}$
$=10^{0.6}$
$=3.981071\ldots$
The louder tool has $4.0$ times the sound intensity.
